course_description:
Total quality management principles and their application in ensuring product quality and safety. International and national food regulatory systems and the development of, and scientific basis for food regulations.

The food industry in Australia is committed to delivering safe, high-quality food to consumers. Ensuring the safety and quality of food is critical not only for public health, but also for environmental sustainability, economic stability and social wellbeing. National and international regulatory bodies work alongside the food industry to establish and enforce standards, policies and monitoring systems, to ensure that foods meet required safety and quality benchmarks.

This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the principles of food safety, quality management and food toxicology. Students will explore key food safety challenges faced by the industry, including biological, chemical, physical and allergenic hazards, and examine the systems used to manage and mitigate these risks. Foundational topics include food allergens, quality assurance systems and the application of Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP) as a central framework for food safety management. The course also introduces risk analysis approaches for evaluating food safety hazards, emphasising the integration of scientific evidence into regulatory decision-making. Furthermore, a strong emphasis is also placed on food toxicity, with dedicated modules on naturally occurring chemical hazards such as phytotoxins and mycotoxins, as well as contaminants including food additives and pesticide residues. Students will develop an understanding of toxicological principles, exposure assessment, and health impacts associated with these substances.

By the end of the course, students will have a well-rounded understanding of modern food safety systems, including the identification, assessment, and management of risks associated with foodborne hazards and toxic compounds.

At the School of Agriculture and Food Sustainability, we are committed to creating an inclusive and empowering learning environment for all students. We value and respect the diverse range of experiences our students bring to their education, and we believe that this diversity is crucial for fostering a rich culture of knowledge-sharing and meaningful exploration. We hold students and staff accountable for actively contributing to establishing a respectful and supportive learning environment.

Bullying, harassment, and discrimination in any form are strictly against our principles and againstﾠ UQ Policy, ﾠand will not be tolerated. If you have any concerns about your experience in this course, we encourage you to tell a member of the course teaching team. Your well-being and a positive learning atmosphere are of utmost importance to us.

Additional timetable information
The outline below describes the modules offered to students over the Semester's teaching weeks:
Each week, there will be a 2-hour lecture and a 2-hour tutorial.
Weeks 1 & 2: Food safety and Food allergens.
Weeks 3 - 8: Quality assurance (QA) in food, and exploring in details relevant food safety management tools including HACCP and Risk analysis, the latter topic delivered by an Industry Expert, with case studies presented in lecture and tutorial sessions.
Weeks 9 - 11: Food Toxicology, including phytotoxins, mycotoxins, food additives, contaminants and pesticides.
Weeks 12 & 13: Food Safety Culture and Future trends in food safety, delivered by an Industry Expert.
Tutorials will commence from Week 1 and students are expected to bring their electronic devices along to work on tutorial activities and assessment tasks scheduled during the tutorial sessions.
All lectures and tutorials will be recorded and available on the course Learn.UQ Ultra site. ﾠ

course_aims: The aim of this course is to introduce students to:

learning_outcomes.description: Apply the principles of Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP) to identify food safety hazards, determine critical control points and develop monitoring and corrective action strategies to ensure the safety and quality of food products.
Use risk analysis approaches to identify, evaluate and manage biological, chemical, physical and allergenic hazards in the food supply chain.
Interpret food regulations, guidelines and codes of practice to evaluate compliance and inform evidence-based decision making in food safety and quality management.
Evaluate foodborne hazards and toxic substances including naturally occurring toxins, contaminants and additives by applying principles of toxicology, exposure assessment and health risk evaluation.

learning_activities.topic: Lectures A series of lectures will be delivered to introduce the concepts and importance of food safety, food allergens and quality assurance (QA) in the food industry. HACCP and predictive microbiology-based food safety management tools will be taught, as well as risk analysis. A detailed week-by-week timetable of lecture topics can be accessed in the Blackboard Learning Resources Folder.
